h1: Business Laptops in India: HP, Lenovo & Acer for Offices
intro:
A business laptop is bought for three years of daily use by someone who cannot afford a morning lost to a slow or broken machine. The purchase looks simple, but the details decide whether it works out: the processor class against the actual workload, enough memory, the right storage, warranty that brings an engineer to the office, and an operating system image that your IT team can deploy without a day of manual setup per machine.

This guide explains how to specify business laptops, how to choose between HP, Lenovo and Acer, how warranty and support are structured, and what to check when buying in India. It is written for the IT head or admin manager who has to equip a team and justify the choice on paper.

On availability: TechZoid lists four HP business notebooks, shown below. Laptops are hardware, quoted to configuration, so the website carries no price for them and a written quotation fixes it. Lenovo and Acer are quoted on request and are not in our catalogue; see the [Lenovo](/brands/lenovo) and [Acer](/brands/acer) pages and use the [enquiry form](/enquiry). Specifications and availability are confirmed on the quotation.

sections.heading: What a business laptop is, and how it differs from a consumer one
sections.markdown:
Consumer and business laptops can look similar on a shelf. The differences show up in management and support, not in the lid:

- **Manageability.** Business ranges are designed to be deployed and administered in numbers, with firmware and driver management and tools your IT team can script.
- **Operating system edition.** Business machines are normally supplied with Windows Pro, which supports joining a domain or Microsoft Entra ID, disk encryption management and group policy. Home editions do not. Check the edition on the quotation. Our article on [Windows 11 Pro versus Enterprise](/blog/windows-11-pro-versus-enterprise-for-business) explains the next step up.
- **Build and service.** Business ranges are generally built for heavier daily use and offer warranty upgrades, though the specifics differ by model and are confirmed on the quotation.
- **Consistency.** A business range is usually refreshed on a predictable cycle, which helps when you buy twenty now and ten more next year and want them to behave alike.

If your staff work mainly in email, Microsoft 365 apps, browsers, ERP and video calls, an office-class laptop is the right tool. Design, CAD and video work belong on a workstation, so read our [CAD software](/cad-software) guide before buying hardware for those roles.

sections.heading: How to choose: processor, memory, storage and display
sections.markdown:
Specify by role, not by one standard for everyone.

- **Processor class.** For office work, a current mainstream Intel Core or AMD Ryzen processor in the mid range is usually enough. A lower tier is false economy if the laptop must last three to four years, because Microsoft 365, browsers and Teams keep growing. Choose a higher tier only for roles that run heavy spreadsheets, local databases or virtual machines.
- **Memory.** 8 GB works for light use but is tight on a Windows machine running several apps and a browser with many tabs. 16 GB is the safer standard for a three-year life. Check whether the memory is soldered or upgradeable, because soldered memory cannot be added to later.
- **Storage.** An SSD is the baseline. Choose capacity by what is kept locally. If files live in OneDrive or on a server, a smaller drive is fine; if staff keep large local data, size up.
- **Display and weight.** For staff who travel, weight and battery matter more than screen size. For desk-based staff, a larger screen is a productivity gain that costs little. Check the screen resolution and whether the panel is described as matte or glossy.
- **Ports and connectivity.** Match them to your docks, monitors and wireless standards, and confirm HDMI or USB-C video if you use external displays.

**The decision rule:** pick two or three standard configurations, for example a general office build and a power-user build, rather than a different laptop per person. That keeps spares, imaging and support simple. Read each configuration out of the quotation, line by line, because model numbers alone often hide differences in processor, memory and storage.

sections.heading: The HP notebooks we list
sections.markdown:
TechZoid lists four HP business notebooks. They are entry-to-mainstream office machines. Each page shows the model and the configuration detail we hold. Because laptops are hardware, we do not publish prices; the price and the exact configuration are confirmed on a [written quotation](/enquiry).

- **[HP 250R G10 Notebook](/products/hp-250r-g10-notebook)** and **[HP 255 G10 Notebook](/products/hp-255-g10-notebook)** are 15-inch class business notebooks for desk-based staff who want a larger screen.
- **[HP 240R G10 Notebook](/products/hp-240r-g10-notebook)** and **[HP 245 G10 Notebook](/products/hp-245-g10-notebook)** are 14-inch class models, easier to carry for staff who move between desks and meeting rooms.

One common difference between the 250R and 240R models and the 255 and 245 models is the processor family: the numbering typically signals an Intel configuration against an AMD one, but check the product page and the quotation for the actual processor, since it varies by configuration. Open each page for the details we hold, and tell us the roles and quantities so we can recommend configurations. If you want a Lenovo or Acer notebook, we quote those on request; they are not listed in our catalogue.

For desktops and workstations, see the [HP Pro 400 G9 Small Form Factor](/products/hp-pro-400-g9-small-form-factor) and the [price list](/price-list).

sections.heading: Warranty, support and operating system imaging
sections.markdown:
**Warranty.** The standard warranty on business laptops is usually a limited term, often one year, and what it covers depends on the model and the region. The practical questions are: is service carry-in, pickup-and-return or onsite; what is the response time; does it cover the battery; and is accidental damage included or an extra? Ask for the warranty type and term to be written in the quotation, and price the upgrade to three years if your laptops are meant to last that long. Do not assume onsite service. Confirm it.

**Operating system.** Confirm the Windows edition, and whether the licence is a preinstalled OEM one that stays with the machine. If you plan to join laptops to your tenant, plan [Microsoft 365 Business Premium](/products/microsoft-365-business-premium) for device management and security alongside them; our guide to [what you already own in Business Premium](/blog/microsoft-365-business-premium-security-you-already-own) explains why.

**Imaging and deployment.** For more than a handful of machines, decide how they will be set up. Options are a standard image deployed by your IT team, a cloud-based provisioning process through your Microsoft tenant, or manual setup. Tell us if you need machines supplied clean or with your image, so that we can raise it with the quotation. Our [endpoint management](/services/endpoint-management) service covers deployment and policy for managed fleets.

**Accessories.** Bags, docks, adapters, monitors and extra chargers add up. List them in the same quotation.

sections.heading: Common mistakes when buying business laptops
sections.markdown:
- **Under-buying memory to hit a unit price.** Eight gigabytes saves a little now and costs productivity for years.
- **Mixing too many models.** Every extra model means another image, another driver set and another spare.
- **Ignoring the warranty type.** A cheap carry-in warranty on a laptop used by a travelling manager can mean weeks without a machine.
- **Buying Home edition by accident.** It cannot be managed the way a business needs. Check the operating system line on the quotation.
- **Forgetting the lifecycle.** Decide the replacement cycle and what happens to old devices, including secure data wiping, before you buy.
- **Skipping protection.** A new laptop on an unmanaged network with no [endpoint security](/antivirus-endpoint-security) is only as safe as the user's next click, and without [backup](/backup-software) the data on it is only as safe as the drive.

sections.heading: Buying notes for India
sections.markdown:
- **Written quotation.** Ask for a written quotation that lists the model, processor, memory, storage, operating system edition, warranty type and term, and quantity. Website information is a guide, and the quotation fixes the specification and the price.
- **GST invoice.** Every TechZoid order is invoiced with GST. Give us your registered entity name and GSTIN before the invoice is raised. GST-registered buyers can usually claim input credit on business purchases; confirm with your accountant.
- **Purchase order.** We accept orders against your purchase order, and can quote laptops with software, security and networking on one PO across brands. See [IT procurement](/services/it-procurement) and [enterprise IT hardware](/enterprise-it-hardware).
- **Delivery and serials.** Ask us to confirm delivery arrangements on the quotation, and keep the serial numbers against the invoice, since warranty claims and asset registers depend on them.
- **Licences with the hardware.** If the order also includes Microsoft 365 or other software, see our guide to [buying genuine Microsoft licences in India](/blog/how-to-buy-genuine-microsoft-licences-in-india).

faqs.question: Which business laptops does TechZoid list?
faqs.answer: Four HP notebooks: the HP 250R G10, HP 255 G10, HP 240R G10 and HP 245 G10. They are hardware, so they are quoted to configuration and the price is confirmed on a written quotation. Lenovo and Acer are quoted on request.

faqs.question: Can you quote Lenovo or Acer laptops?
faqs.answer: Yes, on request. They are not in our catalogue, so send the quantity, processor, memory, storage and warranty you want through the enquiry page and we will respond with a written quotation.

faqs.question: How much memory should a business laptop have?
faqs.answer: For a three-year life on Windows with Microsoft 365, browsers and video calls, 16 GB is the safer standard. 8 GB can work for light use but leaves little headroom. Check whether memory can be upgraded later.

faqs.question: Is onsite warranty included?
faqs.answer: Do not assume so. Warranty type and term vary by model. Ask for the warranty type, term and whether it is onsite, pickup or carry-in to be written in the quotation, and price an upgrade if you want longer cover.

faqs.question: Can the laptops arrive with our own OS image?
faqs.answer: Tell us when you request the quotation. Whether imaging is possible, and on what terms, will be stated on the quotation. For larger fleets, cloud-based provisioning through your Microsoft tenant is another route to consider.

faqs.question: Can I buy laptops, software and a firewall on one purchase order?
faqs.answer: Yes. TechZoid can quote across brands on one purchase order, with a GST invoice. Send the full list and we will return a single written quotation.

faqs.question: Should designers and CAD users get these notebooks?
faqs.answer: Usually not. Office-class notebooks suit email, documents and web apps. CAD, rendering and video work need a workstation with a suitable graphics card and more memory, and the software publisher's system requirements should guide the specification.
